Reverse VAT Calculation: from Gross Price back to Net + VAT

Last updated: 2026-08-23 · Source: European Commission TEDB · 5 min read

A reverse VAT calculation starts from the VAT-inclusive (gross) price and extracts the VAT hidden inside it. Use it whenever a supplier quotes you gross prices, or when you need the VAT content of your own shelf prices before filing.

The formula

Divide the gross price by one plus the rate (as a decimal) to recover the net amount, then subtract to find the VAT: net = gross ÷ (1 + rate/100), VAT = gross − net. The free VAT calculator does this instantly — choose “Gross (extract VAT)”.

Worked examples (from the dataset)

  • Germany, 19%: €119 gross ÷ 1.19 = €100 net, so the VAT is €19. See the VAT calculator for Germany.
  • Ireland, 23%: €123 gross ÷ 1.23 = €100 net, so the VAT is €23. See the VAT calculator for Ireland.
  • Finland, 25.5%: €125.50 gross ÷ 1.255 = €100 net, so the VAT is €25.50. See the VAT calculator for Finland.

The common mistake is taking “19% of the gross” (€119 × 19% = €22.61) — that overstates the VAT, because the 19% applies to the net, not the total. Always divide first.

When sellers need this

Check supplier invoices quoted gross, split marketplace payouts into net revenue plus VAT, or verify shelf prices across countries in the full EU VAT rates table. If you sell digitally across borders, read when the EU One-Stop Shop (OSS) covers your sales next.
